comparisons.peer_summary: The Company has four reportable segments: Data Center (including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, etc.), Client (CPUs, APUs, chipsets for desktops/notebooks), Gaming (discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoCs), and Embedded (embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, SOMs).
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose their semiconductor segment structures with a primary focus on Data Center and AI applications, but they differ in scope. AVGO's Semiconductor Solutions segment is broadly defined to include data center, mobile, set-top box, industrial, and automotive markets plus IP licensing. In contrast, AMD breaks its business into four specific reportable segments (Data Center, Client, Gaming, Embedded). While both highlight AI accelerators and data center solutions, AVGO's definition is more diverse across end-markets (mobile/set-top), whereas AMD's Data Center segment is narrowly focused on server/AI hardware (CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs) without the consumer/mobile breadth of AVGO's segment.

sentences.text: We provide semiconductor solutions for managing the movement of data in data center, service provider, and enterprise networking applications, including AI networking and connectivity.
Our semiconductor solutions segment also includes our IP licensing.

• the Data Center segment, which primarily includes Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerators, server microprocessors (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), accelerated processing units (APUs), data processing units (DPUs), Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs) and Adaptive System-on-Chip (SoC) products for data centers;
• the Embedded segment, which primarily includes embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, System on Modules (SOMs), and Adaptive SoC products.

comparisons.peer_summary: Business is organized into Intel Products, Intel Foundry, and All other; CCG, DCAI, and Intel Foundry are reportable operating segments, while NEX, Altera, and Mobileye are non-reportable segments with selective disclosure.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC disclose their reportable operating segments under Item 8, but their organizational structures and market focuses differ significantly. AVGO defines a single 'Semiconductor Solutions' segment covering diverse applications from data center to mobile and automotive. INTC, conversely, organizes its business into multiple product groups (Intel Products, Intel Foundry) with specific reportable segments including Client Computing Group (CCG), Data Center and AI (DCAI), and Intel Foundry. AVGO's single-segment approach contrasts with INTC's multi-segment disclosure that explicitly separates foundry operations and client computing from its AI/data center focus.

comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA define segments that include data center and networking solutions, but with different product emphases. AVGO's Semiconductor Solutions segment provides 'semiconductor solutions for managing the movement of data in data center, service provider, and enterprise networking applications.' NVDA's Compute & Networking segment includes 'Data Center accelerated computing platform; networking; ... and DGX Cloud.' Both highlight networking and data center infrastructure as key components of their segment definitions, reflecting the semiconductor industry's focus on AI and data infrastructure, though AVGO also includes mobile/industrial markets while NVDA's segment is heavily weighted toward accelerated computing and software.
